content.title: About
content.content: Biryani with meat is a classic Indian dish consisting of fragrant rice cooked with spices, vegetables, and tender pieces of stewed meat (usually lamb or chicken). The dish is known for its rich flavor, vibrant color from turmeric and saffron, and the distinctive aroma of garam masala.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word biryani derives from the Persian “birinj” meaning “fried rice”.
Regional variations abound: Hyderabad biryani often includes cashews, while Delhi versions add yogurt.
Traditionally the dish is cooked in a large clay pot (handi) to lock in aroma.
Biryani is a staple at festivals and family celebrations.
In authentic recipes, the meat is marinated in spices for at least four hours.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice supplies steady‑release energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains beneficial spices
items.content: Turmeric and saffron have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and coriander stimulate bile production and aid digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and rice deliver B1, B3, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Biryani is often seasoned heavily; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Certain spices (e.g., mustard powder) can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑rich due to oil and meat; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Risk of foodborne bacteria
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella or campylobacter contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve biryani hot, often accompanied by a yogurt‑based raita, pickled vegetables, or a fresh salad. Garnish with fried nuts and raisins for added texture and sweetness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftover biryani to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat on the stovetop or in a microwave, adding a splash of water to restore moisture.

fish-flounder-baked-or-broiled-coated.title: Fish, flounder, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Flounder fillet is a delicate white meat from a flat sea fish, commonly baked or broiled after being coated. The coating—often breadcrumbs, spices, and sometimes dairy—creates a crisp crust while keeping the fish moist.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flounder is one of the flattest fish species, lying almost completely on the sea floor.
Its meat is low in fat but high in protein and omega‑3 fatty acids.
Coated flounder is a traditional dish in Northern European and Japanese cuisines.
Flounder can change its skin colour to blend with the seabed.
In the US and Canada the fish is commonly referred to as a “flatfish.”

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 18 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Contains EPA and DHA, which support heart health and brain function.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Approximately 90 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flounder supplies vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, phosphorus and potassium, which aid immune function and bone health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including flounder.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many marine fish, flounder can accumulate mercury and other toxins; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Pre‑coated products often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake the coated fillet at 180 °C for 12‑15 minutes or pan‑fry until golden. Typically the fish is rinsed, patted dry, then dredged in a mixture of breadcrumbs, spices and a little flour. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, or a light yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh flounder in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic, for up to 2 days. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before cooking, check for a strong or ammonia‑like odor—if present, discard.

content.title: About
content.content: Liverwurst (also called liver sausage) is a cooked‑smoked sausage made primarily from pork (sometimes beef) liver, often blended with meat, fat and spices. It has a smooth, slightly sweet flavor and a soft, pâté‑like texture. It is commonly sliced and served as a snack, on sandwiches, or as part of a charcuterie board.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Liverwurst has been produced in Europe since the 17th century and is considered a delicacy in Germany, Austria and Poland.
Traditional recipes include onion, nutmeg, clove and curry, giving it a distinctive aroma.
Some regional varieties add butter for an extra creamy mouthfeel.
Black liverwurst, made with blood, gives the sausage a dark colour and richer taste.
It is often served with mustard, pickles or sauerkraut.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Liver provides highly bioavailable heme iron, supporting blood formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Liverwurst is a good source of vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, which are essential for nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The protein in liver supports muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains polyunsaturated fats
items.content: In moderate amounts it supplies beneficial omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids.

items.title: Vitamin A source
items.content: Liver is one of the richest food sources of vitamin A, important for vision and immune health.

items.title: High cholesterol
items.content: Liverwurst contains a notable amount of cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should limit intake.

items.title: Risk of vitamin A excess
items.content: Excessive consumption of liver can lead to hypervitaminosis A, especially in children and pregnant women.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to pork or pork products may react to liverwurst.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Traditional liverwurst is salty; those monitoring sodium should keep portions moderate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice liverwurst thinly and enjoy on bread, crackers, or with mustard and pickled vegetables. It can also be diced into salads, added to cheese boards, or used as a filling for pastries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep liverwurst refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration or a slimy surface.

content.title: About
content.content: Oranges (Citrus × sinensis) are round, juicy citrus fruits that originated in southern China and Southeast Asia. They have a bright orange rind and segmented flesh with a sweet-tart flavor. Oranges are eaten fresh, juiced, and used in desserts, salads, marmalades, and sauces, and their zest is used for flavoring.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sweet orange is a hybrid of the pomelo and the mandarin.
In warm tropical climates, ripe oranges can stay green on the outside.
Oranges are among the most widely grown tree fruits in the world.
Most oranges have around ten segments, each filled with juice vesicles.
The orange peel contains aromatic oils used in cooking and flavoring.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Oranges are a well-known source of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Provides folate and potassium
items.content: These nutrients support cell function and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Eating the whole fruit adds fiber, which supports normal digestion.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Oranges contain plant compounds such as hesperidin that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Hydrating
items.content: Oranges have a high water content, which makes them refreshing.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acid in oranges may trigger heartburn or reflux in sensitive people and may wear down tooth enamel if consumed very often.

items.title: Juice vs. whole fruit
items.content: Orange juice contains natural sugars and provides less fiber than the whole fruit.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may be allergic to oranges or other citrus fruits.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: Bitter (Seville) oranges can interact with certain medications, similar to grapefruit, and orange juice can affect the absorption of some drugs. People taking prescription medicines should check with a healthcare professional.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oranges can be peeled and eaten in segments, juiced, or added to salads, yogurt, and desserts. The zest can be used in baking and sauces, and the fruit can be turned into marmalade. Eating the whole fruit is a way to get fiber along with the juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Oranges can be kept at room temperature for about a week or refrigerated for several weeks. Store them in a cool, ventilated place and away from moldy fruit. Freshly squeezed juice should be refrigerated and drunk within a couple of days.

rice-brown-with-carrots-and-dark-green-v.title: Brown Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of whole‑grain brown rice, carrots, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach), and added fat to enhance flavor and the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll and high amounts of vitamin K.
Adding a small amount of fat (e.g., olive oil) increases the bioavailability of carotenoids and B‑vitamins.
The dish can be easily prepared in a rice cooker or steamer, preserving most nutrients.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Brown rice and vegetables provide substantial dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted to vitamin A, essential for vision.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Dark green vegetables supply lutein and zeaxanthin, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Steady energy release
items.content: Complex carbohydrates in brown rice release glucose slowly, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Beneficial fats and magnesium contribute to normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to rice.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Added fat raises the calorie count, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Some dark green vegetables (e.g., spinach) are high in oxalates, which can be an issue for people prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Potential heavy metal accumulation
items.content: Improperly grown rice can accumulate cadmium; it is recommended to use trusted sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu, or enjoy it as a standalone vegetarian meal. Garnish with fresh herbs or toasted sesame seeds for extra flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it can be stored for up to 2 months after cooling and placing in a freezer‑safe bag.

content.title: About
content.content: Slush frozen drink is a frozen beverage made from fruit juice, sugar and water, served as fine crystal “snow”. It is popular in summer, offers a bright flavor and a refreshing effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial Slush appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
There are more than 30 flavor variants, from classic cherry to exotic mango and passion fruit.
Special machines simultaneously freeze and stir the mixture, creating tiny crystals.
In some countries Slush is served in glasses with ice, in others in plastic cups with a straw.
Sugar content can reach 10–12 % of the total volume.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water in Slush helps maintain fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Vitamins and Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit juice provides vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells.

items.title: Energy Boost
items.content: Sugar quickly replenishes glucose stores, giving an instant energy lift.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Unlike many sweet drinks, Slush contains virtually no fat.

items.title: Mood Enhancement
items.content: The fresh fruit taste and cold sensation can improve mood and reduce fatigue.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: Some flavors may contain nuts, dairy or artificial flavorings that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Cold Sensitivity
items.content: Drinking large amounts of a cold beverage can cause tooth or stomach discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions often contain preservatives and artificial sweeteners that may not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slush is served in a glass or cup, often with a straw. You can add fresh fruit, mint or lime juice to enhance the flavor. It is recommended to sip slowly to avoid over‑cooling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared Slush should be stored in a freezer at –18 °C for no more than 24 hours. With longer storage the texture may become too hard, so a brief thaw before serving is advisable.

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated cola is a carbonated soft drink with the classic cola flavor from which caffeine has been removed. It retains the sweet‑sour taste, caramel aroma, and spice notes, but lacks the stimulating compound.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeinated cola is popular among people who are sensitive to caffeine but still want the familiar cola taste.
Caffeine is removed using a decaffeination process similar to that used for coffee and tea.
In some countries it is marketed as a more suitable option for children, although it still contains sugar and artificial sweeteners.
The first decaf cola appeared in the 1970s in response to growing demand for stimulant‑free beverages.
Even without caffeine, the drink contains trace amounts of theobromine, a mild stimulant found in cocoa.

items.title: No caffeine
items.content: Avoids typical caffeine effects such as anxiety, increased heart rate, and sleep disturbances.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any carbonated beverage, it contributes to daily fluid intake, though water remains the best source.

items.title: Quick source of carbs
items.content: Contains sugar that can rapidly replenish energy stores, useful in cases of hypoglycemia.

items.title: B‑vitamin fortification
items.content: Some formulations are enriched with niacin, vitamin B6 and B12 to support metabolism.

items.title: Taste satisfaction
items.content: Allows people avoiding caffeine to enjoy the classic cola flavor without compromise.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Regular consumption can contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and increased risk of metabolic diseases.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Diet versions may contain sweeteners that cause individual sensitivities in some consumers.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic components can erode tooth enamel with frequent use.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbonated drinks can cause stomach discomfort, bloating, or heartburn in some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve decaffeinated cola chilled as a standalone drink or in mixed drinks. It can also be used in cooking for marinades, glazes, and desserts where a cola flavor is desired without caffeine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days to maintain flavor and carbonation.

vegetable-and-fruit-juice-drink-with-hig.title: Vegetable and Fruit Juice Drink, High in Vitamin C

content.title: About
content.content: The vegetable‑fruit juice is a blend of fresh vegetables and fruits enriched with a high level of vitamin C (5334 mg/L). The drink retains the natural taste and aroma of its ingredients, providing a quick source of vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vitamin C content is about ten times the daily recommended intake for an adult.
The juice is produced by cold‑pressing, which preserves most of the nutrients.
Combining vegetables (e.g., carrot, beet) with fruits (orange, kiwi) enhances the bioavailability of vitamin C.
The product contains no added sugar, preservatives, or artificial flavors.
Packaged in recyclable PET bottles to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: High vitamin C levels boost the body's defense mechanisms, helping to fight infections.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in the juice neutralize free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, promoting skin elasticity and a healthy complexion.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Fiber from the fruits and vegetables supports intestinal motility and normal digestion.

items.title: Reduced fatigue
items.content: Vitamin C participates in energy metabolism, helping to lessen feelings of tiredness and weakness.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific fruits or vegetables used in the blend.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural fruit sugars can raise the product's glycemic index.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: Vitamin C degrades quickly once the bottle is opened, so it should be consumed within 2‑3 days.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The juice is ready to drink straight from the bottle. It can be enjoyed chilled, added to smoothies, used as a base for cocktails, or poured over salads for extra flavor and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. Keep the cap tightly closed after opening. Shelf life after opening is about 3 days.
